0.title: Every Life a Gift from God
0.overview:
Modern medicine has brought great blessings: cures for diseases, safer childbirth, longer lives and relief from pain. It has also raised questions earlier generations never faced. When does a human life begin? May we create children in laboratories? What should be done with frozen embryos? Should parents test for disabilities before birth? May doctors help a suffering person to die?

The Bible does not mention IVF or genetic testing. But it gives clear principles that apply to them all. Every human being is made in God's image. Human life belongs to God, who gives it and takes it away. We are forbidden to take innocent life. And we are called to love and protect the weak, the unborn, the disabled and the dying.

These questions are not abstract. Many readers have faced them personally: a difficult pregnancy, infertility, a child with a disability, a dying parent. This study tries to speak clearly and compassionately, remembering that the gospel brings forgiveness to those who have made wrong choices and comfort to those facing hard ones.

Five units: (1) The Sanctity of Human Life; (2) Life Before Birth; (3) Infertility, IVF and Embryos; (4) Disability and the Value of Every Life; (5) The End of Life.

1.title: The Sanctity of Human Life
1.overview:
Made in God's image. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them (Gen 1:27). Every human being, from the smallest embryo to the oldest adult, bears God's image. Human worth does not depend on ability, intelligence, health, age, usefulness or wantedness. It depends on God's creation and God's love.

Life belongs to God. See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god beside me; I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal (Deut 32:39). We do not own our lives or anyone else's. Job, losing his children, said, The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD (Job 1:21). The giving and taking of life are God's prerogative.

You shall not murder. The sixth commandment forbids the deliberate killing of innocent human beings (Exod 20:13). After the flood, God explained why: Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed, for God made man in his own image (Gen 9:6). Murder is an attack on God's image.

Protecting the weak. Scripture repeatedly calls God's people to defend those who cannot defend themselves. Open your mouth for the mute, for the rights of all who are destitute (Prov 31:8). The unborn, the disabled and the dying are among the most vulnerable people of all.

Christ and the value of life. The Son of God took human flesh, beginning his human life as an embryo in Mary's womb. He healed the sick, welcomed children, touched lepers and gave his life for sinners. The incarnation affirms the value of human life at every stage.
1.theology:
Personhood: Some modern thinkers argue that only those with certain abilities, such as self-awareness or rationality, are "persons" with full rights. Scripture rejects this. Human beings are persons because God made them in his image, not because of what they can do.

Innocent life: Scripture permits the taking of life in limited cases, such as just punishment by the state (Rom 13:4) and self-defence (Exod 22:2). What it forbids is the deliberate killing of the innocent.

Common grace: Many non-Christians also value human life, because God's law is written on every heart (Rom 2:15). Christians can work alongside others to protect life.
1.examples:
Then: In Egypt, Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn boys. But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but let the male children live (Exod 1:17). They risked their lives to protect the newborn, and God blessed them.

Now: A doctor is pressured by colleagues to take part in a procedure that ends human life. Remembering Exodus 1, she respectfully refuses on grounds of conscience, while continuing to care for her patients with excellence. Her integrity costs her a promotion, but she has a clear conscience before God.

A simple test: Do you value people according to what they can do, or according to who made them?

verseByVerse.quote: And for your lifeblood I will require a reckoning: from every beast I will require it and from man. From his fellow man I will require a reckoning for the life of man. "Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed, for God made man in his own image. And you, be fruitful and multiply, increase greatly on the earth and multiply in it." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: After the flood, God requires a reckoning for human blood. Whoever sheds it will be held accountable, because humans are made in God's image. The value of human life is rooted in God's image, not in human opinion or law.

verseByVerse.quote: "'See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god beside me; I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal; and there is none that can deliver out of my hand. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God declares that he alone kills and makes alive, wounds and heals. No one can deliver from his hand. Life and death belong to God. This truth both humbles us and comforts us: our lives are in his hands.

verseByVerse.quote: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah, "When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women and see them on the birthstool, if it is a son, you shall kill him, but if it is a daughter, she shall live." But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but let the male children live. So the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, "Why have you done this, and let the male children live?" The midwives said to Pharaoh, "Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife comes to them." So God dealt well with the midwives. And the people multiplied and grew very strong. And because the midwives feared God, he gave them families. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Hebrew midwives disobeyed Pharaoh's command to kill baby boys. They feared God more than the king. God dealt well with them and gave them families. Protecting innocent life is worth great risk.

verseByVerse.quote: If you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small. Rescue those who are being taken away to death; hold back those who are stumbling to the slaughter. If you say, "Behold, we did not know this," does not he who weighs the heart perceive it? Does not he who keeps watch over your soul know it, and will he not repay man according to his work? (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Proverbs calls God's people to rescue those being taken away to death. We cannot claim ignorance, because God weighs the heart and knows what we knew. Indifference to innocent suffering is not neutral before God.

1.reflection:
What is the foundation of human worth, according to Scripture?

Why is it important that life belongs to God, not to us?

Who are the most vulnerable people in your society?

Read Proverbs 24:10-12. What does it ask of you?

2.title: Life Before Birth
2.overview:
Known in the womb. Scripture speaks of unborn children as persons known and formed by God. For you formed my inward parts; you knitted me together in my mother's womb (Ps 139:13). God said to Jeremiah, Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you (Jer 1:5). David could say, in sin did my mother conceive me (Ps 51:5), speaking of himself from conception.

John and Jesus. When Mary, newly pregnant with Jesus, visited Elizabeth, who was six months pregnant with John, the baby leaped in her womb (Luke 1:41). Elizabeth spoke of the fruit of your womb and called Mary the mother of my Lord (Luke 1:42-43). Both unborn children are treated as persons. The Son of God himself was once an embryo.

Abortion. Since unborn children are human persons made in God's image, deliberately ending their lives is the taking of innocent human life. It is forbidden by the sixth commandment.

Hard cases. Some pregnancies come from rape. Some involve serious disability. Some threaten the mother's life. These are agonising situations. In cases of rape, the child is still an innocent human life, though the mother needs enormous support and care, and the crime must be reported. Where a pregnancy directly threatens the mother's life, such as an ectopic pregnancy where the child cannot survive, treating the mother to save her life is not the same as deliberately killing the child, and is permitted.

Grace for the guilty. Many women and men have been involved in abortion, often under pressure, in fear or without understanding. Scripture offers full forgiveness through Christ. There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus (Rom 8:1). Churches must offer both truth and grace, and practical support to women facing difficult pregnancies.
2.theology:
Exodus 21:22-25: the views. This law concerns men fighting who strike a pregnant woman so that her children come out. Some read it as a miscarriage, with a fine for the loss, and conclude that the unborn child has lower value. Others read it as a premature birth: a fine if the child survives unharmed, and life for life if there is serious harm.

The verdict: The premature-birth reading is more natural, since the text speaks of children coming out, not of a child dying, and then applies the principle of life for life. Even on the other reading, the passage concerns accidental harm, not deliberate killing. Scripture gives no support to abortion.

The church's response: Christians should support pregnancy centres, adoption and foster care, and care for single mothers. Opposing abortion while neglecting mothers and children is inconsistent with the gospel.
2.examples:
Then: John the Baptist leaped in Elizabeth's womb at the presence of the unborn Christ. Even before birth, he was filled with the Holy Spirit, as the angel had promised (Luke 1:15). God's work in a person's life can begin before birth.

Now: A teenage girl from church becomes pregnant and is terrified. Her parents are angry at first, but her church surrounds her with love. An older couple helps with practical needs; others offer childcare later. She keeps her baby. Years later, she says the church's support saved two lives.

A simple test: How could your church practically support women facing unplanned pregnancies?

verseByVerse.quote: For you formed my inward parts; you knitted me together in my mother's womb. I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; my soul knows it very well. My frame was not hidden from you, when I was being made in secret, intricately woven in the depths of the earth. Your eyes saw my unformed substance; in your book were written, every one of them, the days that were formed for me, when as yet there was none of them. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David praises God for forming him in the womb. God knit him together and saw his unformed substance. Every day of his life was written in God's book before it began. The unborn child is known and loved by God.

verseByVerse.quote: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying, "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God tells Jeremiah that he knew him before forming him in the womb and consecrated him before birth. God's relationship with a person can begin before birth. Jeremiah's calling was already set while he was unborn.

verseByVerse.quote: In those days Mary arose and went with haste into the hill country, to a town in Judah, and she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth. And when Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the baby leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit, and she exclaimed with a loud cry, "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb! And why is this granted to me that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Elizabeth's unborn son leaped for joy at the arrival of Mary, who was carrying the unborn Jesus. Elizabeth was filled with the Spirit and blessed Mary and her child. Both unborn babies are treated as real persons, and one is the Lord.

verseByVerse.quote: "When men strive together and hit a pregnant woman, so that her children come out, but there is no harm, the one who hit her shall surely be fined, as the woman's husband shall impose on him, and he shall pay as the judges determine. But if there is harm, then you shall pay life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burn for burn, wound for wound, stripe for stripe. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This law addresses harm to a pregnant woman during a fight. If her children come out and there is no harm, the offender pays a fine. If there is harm, the penalty is life for life. Many read this as treating the unborn child with the same protection as any other person.

2.reflection:
How do Psalm 139 and Jeremiah 1 shape your view of the unborn?

Why is it significant that the Son of God was once an embryo?

How can the church offer both truth and grace on abortion?

What practical support could you or your church give to women in crisis pregnancies?

3.title: Infertility, IVF and Embryos
3.overview:
The pain of infertility. Scripture is full of women who longed for children: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Hannah, Elizabeth. Rachel cried to Jacob, Give me children, or I shall die! (Gen 30:1). Hannah wept and would not eat, praying in deep distress (1 Sam 1:7-10). Infertility is a real grief, often hidden, and churches should treat it with great compassion.

Children are a gift. Behold, children are a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb a reward (Ps 127:3). Children are given by God, not owed to us. Couples who long for children may pray, seek medical help and trust God's wisdom. Many find joy through adoption, which reflects God's own adoption of us (Eph 1:5).

Medical help. Seeking medical treatment for infertility is not wrong. Doctors can treat many causes. The ethical questions arise with some assisted reproductive technologies, especially IVF.

IVF and embryos. In IVF, eggs are fertilised outside the body, creating embryos, which are then placed in the womb. Often more embryos are created than are used. Some are frozen indefinitely, some destroyed, some used for research. Since embryos are human lives made in God's image, creating them only to discard or freeze them raises serious moral problems.

Third parties. Some techniques bring a third person into the marriage: donor eggs, donor sperm or surrogate mothers. This separates parenthood from the one-flesh union of marriage and raises concerns for children who may never know their biological parent.
3.theology:
IVF: the views. Some Christians reject IVF entirely, arguing that it separates procreation from sexual union. Others accept IVF freely, treating embryos as potential life rather than persons. Many take a middle position: IVF within marriage, using the couple's own eggs and sperm, is permissible if every embryo created is treated as a child, with none deliberately destroyed.

The verdict: The middle position is wise. IVF is not forbidden in itself, but every embryo is a human life. Couples should create only as many embryos as they intend to implant, refuse the destruction of embryos and avoid donor gametes and surrogacy, which bring a third party into the marriage. Frozen embryos already in existence can be given a chance at life through embryo adoption. Christians who have used IVF in other ways should find grace, not condemnation.

Trusting God: Not every couple will have children, whatever they do. God's love does not depend on fertility, and a childless life can be fruitful in God's kingdom (Isa 56:3-5).
3.examples:
Then: Hannah poured out her soul before the LORD at the temple. Eli thought she was drunk. When she explained, he blessed her. God answered her prayer with Samuel, and she gave him back to the LORD (1 Sam 1:12-28). Her grief became praise.

Now: A couple who have struggled with infertility for years decide to pursue IVF. They talk with their pastor and doctor and decide to create only a small number of embryos, intending to implant all of them. When they have one child, they still have two frozen embryos, which they later implant too. Every child is welcomed as a gift.

A simple test: Is there someone in your church struggling with infertility who needs care and prayer?

verseByVerse.quote: After they had eaten and drunk in Shiloh, Hannah rose. Now Eli the priest was sitting on the seat beside the doorpost of the temple of the LORD. She was deeply distressed and prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly. And she vowed a vow and said, "O LORD of hosts, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your servant and remember me and not forget your servant, but will give to your servant a son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall touch his head." As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli observed her mouth. Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, and her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli took her to be a drunken woman. And Eli said to her, "How long will you go on being drunk? Put your wine away from you." But Hannah answered, "No, my lord, I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD. Do not regard your servant as a worthless woman, for all along I have been speaking out of my great anxiety and vexation." Then Eli answered, "Go in peace, and the God of Israel grant your petition that you have made to him." And she said, "Let your servant find favor in your eyes." Then the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Hannah prayed in deep distress, weeping bitterly and making a vow. Eli misjudged her, but she explained that she had been pouring out her soul to the LORD. He blessed her, and she went away no longer sad. Honest prayer brought peace even before the answer came.

verseByVerse.quote: Behold, children are a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb a reward. Like arrows in the hand of a warrior are the children of one's youth. Blessed is the man who fills his quiver with them! He shall not be put to shame when he speaks with his enemies in the gate. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Children are a heritage and reward from the LORD, like arrows in the hand of a warrior. They are gifts, not rights or products. Every child, however conceived, is a gift from God to be welcomed and loved.

verseByVerse.quote: When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, she envied her sister. She said to Jacob, "Give me children, or I shall die!" Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel, and he said, "Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Rachel envied her sister and demanded children from Jacob. Jacob, angry, replied that he was not in the place of God, who had withheld children from her. Children are ultimately given by God. Rachel's later use of a servant to bear children brought further conflict.

verseByVerse.quote: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes, with the princes of his people. He gives the barren woman a home, making her the joyous mother of children. Praise the LORD! (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God raises the poor from the dust and gives the barren woman a home, making her the joyous mother of children. This psalm celebrates God's power to change circumstances. It is a prayer of hope for those who long for children.

3.reflection:
How can churches better support couples facing infertility?

Why do embryos raise moral questions in IVF?

What are the concerns about bringing a third party into reproduction?

How does God's adoption of us give meaning to human adoption?

4.title: Disability and the Value of Every Life
4.overview:
God's sovereignty. When Moses protested that he was not eloquent, God answered, Who has made man's mouth? Who makes him mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, the LORD? (Exod 4:11). Disability is not outside God's purposes. This does not make disability good in itself, but it means that no life is a mistake.

Not a punishment. The disciples asked Jesus whether a man born blind was being punished for his sin or his parents'. Jesus answered, It was not that this man sinned, or his parents, but that the works of God might be displayed in him (John 9:3). Disability is not evidence of special sin.

Welcomed at the King's table. King David sought out Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, who was lame in both feet, and invited him to eat at the king's table always, like one of the king's sons (2 Sam 9:11). David's kindness reflects God's grace to the weak.

Indispensable. Paul says that in the church, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable (1 Cor 12:22). People with disabilities are not burdens to the church but gifts to it.

Prenatal testing. Prenatal testing can help prepare parents and doctors to care for a child. But in many places, it leads to the abortion of children diagnosed with disabilities. Christians should value every child, whatever the diagnosis, and support families caring for children with disabilities.

The resurrection hope. In the new creation, every disability will be healed. Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then shall the lame man leap like a deer (Isa 35:5-6).
4.theology:
Weakness and grace: God often displays his power in weakness (2 Cor 12:9). People with disabilities often teach the church dependence, patience and grace.

Caring for carers: Parents and families caring for people with severe disabilities often carry heavy, lifelong burdens. The church should offer practical help, respite and friendship.

Inclusion in the church: Churches should make it possible for people with disabilities to worship, belong and serve, considering access, communication and pastoral care.
4.examples:
Then: Jesus told a parable of a great banquet. When the invited guests refused, the master said, bring in the poor and crippled and blind and lame (Luke 14:21). God's kingdom welcomes those the world overlooks.

Now: A couple is told during pregnancy that their baby has a serious genetic condition, and they are offered an abortion. They decline. Their church supports them through the birth and beyond. Their daughter's life is shorter than most, but full of love. They say she taught their whole church what it means to be valued simply for who you are.

A simple test: How welcoming is your church to people with disabilities and their families?

verseByVerse.quote: But Moses said to the LORD, "Oh, my Lord, I am not eloquent, either in the past or since you have spoken to your servant, but I am slow of speech and of tongue." Then the LORD said to him, "Who has made man's mouth? Who makes him mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, the LORD? Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you shall speak." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Moses complained of his slow speech. God reminded him that he made every mouth, and every sense or lack of sense. Then he promised to be with Moses' mouth and teach him what to say. God's purposes are not limited by human weakness.

verseByVerse.quote: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth. And his disciples asked him, "Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?" Jesus answered, "It was not that this man sinned, or his parents, but that the works of God might be displayed in him. We must work the works of him who sent me while it is day; night is coming, when no one can work. As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world." Having said these things, he spit on the ground and made mud with the saliva. Then he anointed the man's eyes with the mud and said to him, "Go, wash in the pool of Siloam" (which means Sent). So he went and washed and came back seeing. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The disciples assumed blindness was a punishment for sin. Jesus rejected this. The man was blind so that God's works might be displayed. Jesus then healed him. Disability is not a mark of special guilt, and God works through it.

verseByVerse.quote: And David said, "Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?" Now there was a servant of the house of Saul whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David. And the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he said, "I am your servant." And the king said, "Is there not still someone of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to him?" Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan; he is crippled in his feet." The king said to him, "Where is he?" And Ziba said to the king, "He is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, at Lo-debar." Then King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, at Lo-debar. And Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came to David and fell on his face and paid homage. And David said, "Mephibosheth!" And he answered, "Behold, I am your servant." And David said to him, "Do not fear, for I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan, and I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you shall eat at my table always." And he paid homage and said, "What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog such as I?" Then the king called Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's grandson. And you and your sons and your servants shall till the land for him and shall bring in the produce, that your master's grandson may have bread to eat. But Mephibosheth your master's grandson shall always eat at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants. Then Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so will your servant do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table, like one of the king's sons. And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. And all who lived in Ziba's house became Mephibosheth's servants. So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate always at the king's table. Now he was lame in both his feet. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David sought someone from Saul's house to show kindness for Jonathan's sake. He found Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, restored his land and gave him a permanent place at the king's table. This is a picture of the gospel: the weak welcomed to the King's table by grace.

verseByVerse.quote: The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you." On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and on those parts of the body that we think less honorable we bestow the greater honor, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty, which our more presentable parts do not require. But God has so composed the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it, that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another. If one member suffers, all suffer together; if one member is honored, all rejoice together. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you." The weaker members are indispensable, and the less honourable are given greater honour. God has composed the body so that all members care for one another. People with disabilities are essential to the church.

4.reflection:
How does Exodus 4:11 shape your view of disability?

How does Jesus correct the disciples' assumption in John 9?

What does Mephibosheth's story teach about God's grace?

How could your church better welcome people with disabilities and support their families?

5.title: The End of Life
5.overview:
A time to die. For everything there is a season... a time to be born, and a time to die (Eccl 3:1-2). Death will come to all, and modern medicine cannot prevent it forever. Christians face death with hope, not denial, and they need not fight it at any cost.

Euthanasia and assisted suicide. Some argue that suffering people should be allowed or helped to end their lives. Scripture forbids deliberately ending innocent life, including one's own (Exod 20:13). Euthanasia and assisted suicide, even when motivated by compassion, take into human hands what belongs to God. They also put pressure on the elderly, sick and disabled to feel they are a burden.

Allowing death and causing death. Christians are not required to accept every possible treatment. It is right to decline or withdraw treatments that are burdensome and offer little hope, allowing a disease to take its course. It is right to give good pain relief, even if it may shorten life as a side effect. The line is between allowing death and deliberately causing it.

Palliative care. Excellent care of the dying, relieving pain and providing comfort, companionship and spiritual support, is a Christian calling. The modern hospice movement grew largely out of Christian conviction. Dying people need presence, not abandonment.

Suffering and meaning. Suffering at the end of life is real and hard. But it is not meaningless. For this light momentary affliction is preparing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison (2 Cor 4:17). God can use even the final days of life for good: reconciliation, witness and preparation for glory.
5.theology:
Our bodies belong to God: You are not your own, for you were bought with a price (1 Cor 6:19-20). We do not have the right to end our own lives, even when they are hard.

Advance planning: Christians should consider making their wishes known about end-of-life care, through conversations with family and written directives, in line with biblical principles.

The Death, Dying and Heaven study: That study covers preparing for death, grief and the Christian hope more fully.
5.examples:
Then: King Saul, wounded in battle, asked his armour-bearer to kill him. The armour-bearer refused, and Saul fell on his own sword (1 Sam 31:4). Later, an Amalekite claimed to have killed Saul at his request, and David had him executed for raising his hand against the LORD's anointed (2 Sam 1:9-16). Assisting a death, even at the dying person's request, was treated as killing.

Now: A Christian family faces their father's final illness. The doctors propose aggressive treatment with little chance of success. After prayer and discussion, the family chooses palliative care. Their father's pain is well managed. He spends his final weeks at home, reconciling with his estranged son and reading Psalms with his grandchildren. He dies peacefully.

A simple test: Have you discussed your wishes for end-of-life care with your family?

verseByVerse.quote: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up what is planted; (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Preacher reminds us that everything has its season under heaven, including birth and death. We do not control the times. Accepting that there is a time to die is not giving up on life; it is trusting God with its boundaries.

verseByVerse.quote: Then Job arose and tore his robe and shaved his head and fell on the ground and worshiped. And he said, "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked shall I return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD." In all this Job did not sin or charge God with wrong. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Job, having lost his children and possessions, tore his robe, fell on the ground and worshipped. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD. In all this Job did not sin or charge God with wrong. Life and death are in God's hands.

verseByVerse.quote: So we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day. For this light momentary affliction is preparing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison, as we look not to the things that are seen but to the things that are unseen. For the things that are seen are transient, but the things that are unseen are eternal. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Our outer self is wasting away, but our inner self is renewed day by day. Present affliction is light and momentary compared with eternal glory. We look not at what is seen, which is transient, but at what is unseen and eternal. This hope sustains believers through the end of life.

verseByVerse.quote: Then David said to the young man who told him, "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?" And the young man who told him said, "By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear, and behold, the chariots and the horsemen were close upon him. And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, 'Here I am.' And he said to me, 'Who are you?' I answered him, 'I am an Amalekite.' And he said to me, 'Stand beside me and kill me, for anguish has seized me, and yet my life still lingers.' So I stood beside him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord." Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him. And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for the people of the LORD and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword. And David said to the young man who told him, "Where do you come from?" And he answered, "I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite." David said to him, "How is it you were not afraid to put out your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?" Then David called one of the young men and said, "Go, execute him." And he struck him down so that he died. And David said to him, "Your blood be on your head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I have killed the LORD's anointed.'" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: An Amalekite claimed to have killed the wounded Saul at Saul's own request. David did not treat it as mercy. He held the man responsible for destroying the LORD's anointed. Taking a life at the person's request was still treated as killing.
